evidence.recipientRole: Uniswap V2 WETH/SHIELD pair (registered automatedMarketMakerPairs entry)
evidence.taxDestinationRole: the SHIELD token contract itself, which accumulates fees for later swap-back

derivation.formula: fees = floor(amount * sellTotalFees / 100); transferToRecipient = amount - fees

evidence.computation: One transfer of 244827287308804937041677 SHIELD out of the USDC/SHIELD pool emits two Transfer events with the same sender: 230137650070276640819177 to the WETH/SHIELD pair and 14689637238528296222500 to the token contract. floor(244827287308804937041677 * 6 / 100) == 14689637238528296222500 EXACTLY, and amount - fees == 230137650070276640819177 EXACTLY, so the measured tax is exactly 600 bps with no rounding residue. This is the sell side; buyTotalFees is also 6.

onChainGetters.note: Fee getters are whole percent, not bps: sellTotalFees() == 6 means 6%, confirmed by the exact replay above.

note: 6% tax on both buys and sells, charged only against registered automatedMarketMakerPairs entries. The WETH/SHIELD pair 0xba22211b… is registered; the USDC/SHIELD pool 0xf7dc64ad… is not. That asymmetry makes SHIELD quote as a persistently mispriced routing intermediate: a router can price USDC->SHIELD untaxed and SHIELD->WETH untaxed, but execution charges 6% on the WETH leg, so the delivered amount falls below the quoted minimum. No arbitrageur can close the gap either, because closing it costs the same 6%. Failure modes by position in a router path: (1) SHIELD as INPUT or INTERMEDIATE — the destination pair receives only 94% of amountSent, so the pool's constant-product check reverts or the next leg under-delivers; (2) SHIELD as TERMINAL OUTPUT — the user receives 94% of the quoted amountOut, silently violating minAmountOut. Both are unsafe; the router blocks all positions equally.
